extracted.intended_audience: patent prosecutors, patent drafters, and inventors of computer-implemented/software inventions (U.S. practice)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for drafting and prosecuting patent claims for computer-implemented inventions so they survive 35 U.S.C. §101/Alice challenges; focuses on tying software functionality to particular hardware and showing technical improvements. Useful to patent attorneys and applicants preparing specifications, drawings, and claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid claims directed to an 'abstract idea'
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims that are directed to fundamental economic practices or abstract ideas (e.g., 'intermediated settlement' or 'risk hedging') are not patent-eligible under 35 U.S.C. §101.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abstract ideas are excluded because they would provide a monopoly over an idea and preempt the basic tools of science and technology. Determine whether claimed subject matter is a fundamental economic practice or otherwise an abstract idea before drafting or during prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do more than implement an idea on a generic computer
rubrics_metrics.description: It is necessary to do more than simply implement a principle on a physical machine such as a generic computer to make a claim patent-eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide an improvement in computer technology or an improvement in another technology to transform an abstract idea into a patent-eligible invention. Merely reciting a generic computer performing conventional steps is insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim specific hardware producing a particular outcome
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims that tie functionality to particular hardware producing a particular outcome are more likely to be patent-eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor claims covering functionality linked with a specific structure rather than business procedures performed by a general-purpose computer. Recite hardware elements that provide meaningful limitations rather than generic labels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid 'token' or generic computer components
rubrics_metrics.description: Using generic terms like 'data processing system,' 'communications controller,' or 'data storage unit' as mere placeholders does not make a claim patentable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are considered 'token' components and do not provide patentability. Instead, describe particular hardware or how components are structured and interact in a non-generic way.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recite particular hardware components where appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim particular hardware components (e.g., a particular GPU, specialized device, or memory configured in a new way) to tie the invention to a machine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For example, for graphics technologies recite a particular GPU or memory configured to improve performance; for streaming video characterize operations as performed by specialized devices in an apparatus that interact to process and manage the data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasize hardware structure or distinctive interactions among elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Elements should indicate a particular structure or be claimed to interact in a distinctive way to show the claimed invention is not merely functional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Either claim the elements themselves to indicate a particular structure, or claim that they are structured to interact in a distinctive way that provides technical advantages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasize real-world, observable effects rather than pure information processing
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims should highlight real-world, observable effects or useful results produced by the software instead of just processing information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Showing concrete, observable outcomes helps demonstrate a technological application rather than an abstract informational process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Draft method claims that tie operations to configured hardware
rubrics_metrics.description: Claiming an inventive concept as a method claim that emphasizes operations performed by specific types of hardware configured to perform those operations can help address infringers and meet Alice requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Method claims should describe that steps are performed by hardware that is configured to perform operations constituting an overall technological approach to achieving a useful result with a computer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure system and computer-readable medium claims recite specific hardware
rubrics_metrics.description: System and computer-readable medium claims that fail to recite specific hardware are vulnerable to §101 rejection (as happened in Alice).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: System/medium claims should recite non-generic hardware or structural limitations rather than abstract functionality stored on or executed by unspecified machines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include comprehensive drawings, hardware implementations, architectures, and flowcharts
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare specification drawings and flowcharts that show examples of hardware implementations and architectures and specify how hardware is involved in performing method operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comprehensive drawings and flowcharts provide material to support claims and arguments during prosecution and can show how the claimed invention involves specific hardware or improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Draft the disclosure to emphasize specific hardware structures and alternatives
rubrics_metrics.description: The written description should emphasize specific hardware structures that implement claimed functionality and discuss multiple alternative examples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss multiple alternatives and implementation examples to create prosecution avenues and supply fallback claim language tying functionality to particular machines or structures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim software via specialized device/apparatus language when helpful
rubrics_metrics.description: For software inventions, characterizing steps as operations by specialized components or devices in an apparatus may tie the invention to particular machines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E.g., for a user interface on a mobile device, claim specialized components that interact to receive input, process it, and provide output, rather than only reciting steps performed by 'a processor.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer claiming inventive concept as method claims to address infringers
rubrics_metrics.description: It is often helpful to claim an inventive concept as a method claim to address potential infringers while also showing hardware involvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Method claims emphasizing hardware-configured operations can be tailored to relevant infringers and may be more effective in litigation/ enforcement contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventions directed to computer architectures should claim elements and interactions that provide advantages
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims to processor, memory, or network designs that specifically claim hardware elements and their interaction to obtain advantages are less likely to be affected by Alice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on specific hardware elements and how their interaction yields technical advantages, not merely reciting abstract functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid relying on token computing hardware to overcome §101
rubrics_metrics.description: Merely including token computing hardware does not overcome an abstract idea rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Token references to hardware (e.g., adding 'a computer' without meaningful structural or functional specificity) are insufficient; include meaningful hardware-based limitations or improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be cautious claiming automation of non-computer procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Automating procedures that could be carried out without a computer (even if laborious) may be difficult to patent under Alice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show that the claimed automation provides a technical improvement or specific hardware implementation rather than merely automating a human-performed or conventional business process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipate increased §101 rejections for pending patents and prepare strategies
rubrics_metrics.description: Alice may lead to an increase in non-statutory subject matter rejections for pending patent applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strategies include amending claims to recite particular hardware components, emphasizing hardware-performed functionality in the specification, and preparing alternative claim sets and disclosure to support prosecution responses.
